input.old_string:
- **Writing generated content into a size-capped GitHub API field** (an issue or PR body) —
  budget it explicitly, in two tiers: an always-complete compact summary plus best-effort detail
  rationed to a byte budget with an explicit omitted-count, never a single unbounded write that
  can 422 outright at the ~64KB cap. `growth-dedup`'s brief rendered 350KB against that limit and
  would have failed the run at its first step.
input.new_string:
- **Writing generated content into a size-capped GitHub API field** (an issue or PR body) —
  budget it explicitly, in two tiers: an always-complete compact summary plus best-effort detail
  rationed to a byte budget with an explicit omitted-count, never a single unbounded write that
  can 422 outright at the ~64KB cap. `growth-dedup`'s brief rendered 350KB against that limit and
  would have failed the run at its first step.

- **Writing a generated title whose naive content scales with a variable-length list** (a PR
  title, a notification headline) — collapse the list to a count and keep the per-item detail in
  the body. A title is a summary surface, not a second body, and grows unreadable exactly where a
  long list makes every character compete for space (#1048).

- **Preflighting a required grant or permission** — a probe is only as good as the environment it
  runs against; where the failure is conditional (a scope that 403s only under a specific
  condition, e.g. a private repo), a probe run where that condition isn't met reports a
  false-positive pass. Prefer attributing a real observed 403 to the permission that would fix it
  over guessing from an unrepresentative probe (#1052).

- **Introducing a finer-grained classification of an existing catch-all state** — default
  whatever an older or unaware writer produces (or a future writer's not-yet-known category) to
  the most conservative member of the new set, not the most lenient. An unlabelled park now reads
  as the blocking `failure` lane rather than a soft one, so a writer that predates the split fails
  safe instead of silently landing in a lane nobody watches (#1051).

  never written at all if the kill lands first (#1051).

- **Building or extending a simulator for a stateful engine mechanism** — model what the real
  engine's code actually *writes* (the artifact), never the rule's stated *intent*. A sim that
  advances state on every transition matching the rule's description, rather than only where the
  real engine leaves a mark, is correct by construction and blind to exactly the silent paths
  where the two diverge — which is where the bug lived (an episode-boundary livelock, #925).

- **Asserting a mid-run invariant in a simulator or test** — capture it at the exact moment the
  state holds, not after the run continues past it. A check re-queued before an item had ever left
  a state asserted over an item that never actually failed; by the end of the run normal
  convergence had already cleared the evidence the assertion meant to catch (#1054).

- **A test that derives its answer by walking git history** (which imports are still fielded, from
  trunk) — guard explicitly against a shallow clone and fail loudly rather than silently evaluate
  over whatever partial history happens to be present. A shallow checkout would otherwise let the
  test pass vacuously exactly when the real answer needs history it doesn't have (#1013).

### 2026-08-20 — growth-extract, work item #1035 (PR #1083, squash-merged `cf5844c`)

**15 lessons added, 2 refinements to standing rules**, all into `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`. Nothing outside the local packs.

**Activity half** — window: 26 substantive commits, 28 merged PRs (diff + review discussion read whole: #1082 #1081 #1077 #1076 #1067 #1071 #1068 #1070 #1063 #1060 #1062 #1011 #1059 #1056 #1007 #1054 #975 #1052 #1053 #1051 #1048 #1047 #1042 #1027 #1028 #1013 #1008 #1024), 3 touched PRs (#1031 #1021 #1020 — all zero-comment/machine-authored, nothing durable), 12 touched issues (mostly routine tidy-issues status chatter or already-captured points — nothing durable except one below).

- Permission checks off a GitHub payload use the collaborators-permission API, never `author_association` (#1067)
- A pack rename's config-key fix doesn't reach a member's own already-committed config — the reader must resolve both spellings permanently (#1081)
- A self-diagnosing check must not gate its own relevance on the single signal it exists to catch (#1060)
- Assert a simulator/test invariant at the exact moment the state holds, not after the run continues past it (#1054)
- A doc reached only via a link chain, wanted at authoring time, converts to a skill (#975)
- A check's `doc:` field has no reader — verify it by hand on every file move (#975)
- A preflight probe is only as good as the (possibly unrepresentative) environment it runs in — prefer an observed 403 (#1052)
- A diagnostic verdict from a subprocess with a kill ceiling goes to stdout, never a file written at exit (#1051)
- A new finer-grained classification defaults unaware/legacy input to its most conservative member (#1051)
- A generated title collapses a variable-length list to a count; detail stays in the body (#1048)
- JSON anchored-text patching has an exception: a target nested inside an array-within-an-object needs a structural rewrite (#1042)
- A single timeout bound covering two different waits needs splitting, and a give-up message must never read as a verdict on the work (#1027)
- A git-history-walking test needs an explicit shallow-clone guard (#1013)
- Pipeline stages chained via `after:` should re-derive world state in each precondition, narrowing `on_interrupt` to the one non-idempotent stage (#1073, touched issue — review discussion on an in-flight design)
- Refined the #1001 report-card rule: check whether a metric is stamp-derived before windowing it — a steady population can misread as declining (#1008)

**Conversation half** — fresh pass over the 32 captures since the prior run (2026-08-19T0347Z–2026-08-20T0011Z); hindsight re-read of the branch's oldest 24h (2026-07-19/20, 6 captures).

- Verify a design doc's stated architectural rationale against current code before repeating it, especially once already corrected once — provenance on #1069
- An owner reversing a standing decision needs a full purge of every place the old decision is stated, not just an answer to the immediate question — provenance on #364 (hindsight window)

**Below the bar, deduped out:** two recurrences of already-captured rules (#1010 build-a-pack-vs-scheduler-core, #1026 platform-setting-before-diagnosis) — flagged as re-occurrences, not new lessons, since the existing entries already cover them; a background-sleep/re-poll pattern (#1030) — already covered by the standing "you are sleeping and calling it polling" guard; several weaker candidates from PR review bodies (context-duplication across writer stages, a migration-record-vs-rehearsal-fixture nuance) judged too close to existing rules to add separately.

**Upgrade pass (prose-to-checks), this run's own additions only:** no conversions. Fourteen of fifteen are judgment/design calls with no static repo signature. One — the check-`doc:`-field-never-verified lesson — has a plausible static signature (scan rule modules' `doc:` values, assert each resolves) but needs a custom rule module rather than a declarative pattern; left as prose for the weekly `prose-to-checks-sweep`'s reviewed PR rather than building it under this run's auto-merge.

**Retention prune:** not run — `retention_days` unset for this repo (capture-only adoption).

Verification before opening: `check_the_work` clean; targeted tests (`canon-curation` pack-version-bumped, `claudinite-growth` suite, 123 tests) green.
